prompt: A plain HeaterModel broadcasts "target" and "on" property changes. Register one PropertyChangeListener that keeps two labels in sync and counts the events that actually arrive.
explanation: PropertyChangeSupport is the observer plumbing used all over Java: the model knows nothing about the GUI, it just fires named events, and any number of listeners can subscribe. One listener can serve several properties by branching on evt.getPropertyName(). Because firePropertyChange skips the call when the old and new values are equal, a listener that counts arriving events naturally ignores no-op writes.
hints: PropertyChangeListener is a functional interface, so a lambda works: model.addPropertyChangeListener(evt -> { ... }).
evt.getPropertyName() returns "target" or "on"; compare with "target".equals(...) so the order of the operands cannot cause a null problem.
evt.getNewValue() is an Object -- concatenating it with " C" is enough for the target label, but the on/off label needs a cast to Boolean.
